method: three fresh blind reviewers per round (Claude subagents), five shuffled levels to match to the level descriptions; A/B: this round vs the last at L2 and L4, sides randomised

rounds.change: first build: bloom, ozone cracks as noise contours then short dashes, dock rash, dust, mildew; webbing fade, fuzz, grit, fray, mildew
rounds.ab: vs main: not run (main's levels differ only by a grey lift)
rounds.notes: cracks read as bark or a barcode, also on a kept boat (L3 looked worse than L2); webbing read as a flat slab; L0/L1 hard to tell

rounds.change: cracks fewer, kinked, slanted, mostly on a left boat and on black rubber; thinner matt dock-rash streaks; warp ribs on the webbing; browner fade, paler fuzz
rounds.notes: every reviewer swapped L2 and L3 (the hazy club boat read as the kept one)

rounds.change: dock rash and dust follow dirt (care cleans the marks off), a kept boat's rubber satin from protectant (roughness 0.45), the webbing's weft crossing the ribs

ab.L2: 0 of 3 (all called the pair nearly identical)

rounds.notes: L2/L3 now right for all three; the one miss is an L0/L1 swap

material: rub rail: rubber for most reviewers at L0-L2, 'bark or cork' at L4; grey PVC rail: yes; webbing strap: no in every round (a ribbed plank or mat: no thickness, no stitching or selvedge in the swatch)
least_real: the L4 cracks and mildew specks read as a decal repeated over all three parts
the strap reads as a flat ribbed sheet
the sky's reflections on the rail read as decals (the renderer's crisp environment lobes)
